reason: The finding's core evidence is false. I extracted the leaderboard_rows from e10_watch 20260929T0513Z, 0641Z and 0713Z (R32-A2 awk). Exactly 3 teams are above us at 0713Z that were not at 0513Z (our rank 133 -> 136, count 53, 0.959 in both), and all 3 are at 0.960, not in the 0.959 block: Miz 16758945 (0.958 -> 0.960), Boopathi Raja 16775607 (0.959 below us -> 0.960), Asan Ashirov 16887065 (0.956 -> 0.960). The count of teams at >= 0.960 went 116 -> 120, and the 0.959 block shrank 22 -> 20. A file that displays 0.959 cannot pass a 0.960 team. So for exp89p at 0.959, compare(0513Z, S1) and compare(0713Z, S1) give the same k, and there is no bias toward 0 on the current data. That a newer S0 is at least as sensitive (a superset) is true in principle, but R32-A2 (03:56Z) already sets S0 = the NEWEST snapshot with the right count; R34-A1's '0513Z' is only an example. The remaining exposure is small: a team would have to enter between us (#136) and #135 Amin after 07:13Z, and exp89p's unrounded score would have to land inside that gap. The LB-lag half covers an event that has never been seen (the counts were already up at the 21:42Z and 12:14Z headers). Its 'never MASKED on +0' clause quietly rewrites R34-A1 ('exactly +1, otherwise MASKED') on finals day. Nothing is gained on private/unseen embryos: the finding only changes how finely we read a sub-rounding difference on the public ~29% embryo.

realistic_gain: ~0. Zero difference in k on the snapshots through 07:13Z. The lag guard covers an event not yet observed and costs at most 1 LB call. No effect on private score.
